covering letter = a letter sent with a CV to explain why you want the job
reference = a statement from a teacher or employer about you
qualifications = exams or certificates that show what you can do
training course = a short programme that teaches job skills
work experience = a short time in a real workplace while you are still at school
paid job = work that you receive money for
unpaid work = work you do without money, often to gain skills
minimum wage = the lowest hourly pay allowed by law
pocket money job = light work a teenager does for extra money
working hours = the times you are expected to be at work
flexitime = a system where you can choose when to start and finish
night shift = work that happens during the night
day off = a day when you do not have to work
holiday pay = money you still receive when you are on holiday from work
sick pay = money you receive when you cannot work because you are ill
clock in = to record the time you start work
clock out = to record the time you finish work
promotion = a move to a better, higher job in the same company
raise = an increase in pay
fire = to make someone leave their job because of their work or behaviour
